plan.description: Strongest cloud model on every placement unit: gpt-5.5-cloud

Cost/latency-reduced hybrid: use gpt-4.1-mini for high-frequency routing and initial tool-capable query control, keep gpt-5.5 for user-facing final answer quality, and move low-frequency question rewriting to local.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: Requires structured output and branch control but is not user-facing. gpt-4.1-mini supports structured output and should substantially reduce cloud cost and latency versus gpt-5.5 on the 74 baseline invocations while preserving enough routing quality for a first hybrid test.
rationale.generate_answer: Final answer generation is user-facing and directly drives exact match/F1, so retain the strongest model to protect answer quality on the 32 answer-generation invocations.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: This is the highest-frequency unit and requires tool calling plus branch control. gpt-4.1-mini supports tool calling with a much larger context window and much lower cost than gpt-5.5, making it the main cost/latency trade-off to evaluate.
rationale.rewrite_question: Rewrite is non-user-facing, no tool or structured output required, and relatively low frequency in the baseline. qwen-local has sufficient context and zero cloud cost, so this probes whether local rewriting can reduce the baseline's costly/slow rewrite path without risking endpoint capability violations.

plan.description: Probe a lower-cost all-mini cloud configuration, keeping capable cloud endpoints for tool calling and structured routing while replacing expensive final-answer generation with gpt-4.1-mini to test whether candidate-1's quality gains came mainly from improved routing/retrieval rather than gpt-5.5 answer synthesis.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: Candidate-1 improved exact match and F1 while using gpt-4.1-mini for this structured branch-control unit, so keep mini here to preserve the faster, cheaper retrieval sufficiency routing that appears adequate.
rationale.generate_answer: Candidate-1's largest remaining cloud cost was gpt-5.5 on generate_answer ($0.809 of $0.914). Switching this user-facing step to gpt-4.1-mini tests a major cost reduction while still using a cloud model with large context; answer quality may drop, but per-example results suggest routing/retrieval changes contributed strongly to candidate-1's gains.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: This is the highest-frequency tool-calling branch-control unit. Candidate-1 showed gpt-4.1-mini met the required tool capability and substantially reduced latency/cost versus the baseline, so retain it.
rationale.rewrite_question: Candidate-1 produced no rewrite_question invocations but assigning qwen-local remains capability-safe for this non-user-facing, non-structured, no-tool rewrite path and keeps any rare rewrite attempts at zero cloud cost.

plan.description: Quality-recovery hybrid: keep the empirically strong and cheap gpt-4.1-mini routing/query-control setup from candidates 1-2, restore gpt-5.5 only for final answer generation, and switch rewrite_question from local to gpt-4.1-mini to directly test whether a capable low-cost cloud rewriter improves any rare rewrite path without returning to the expensive all-gpt-5.5 baseline.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: Previously evaluated candidates using gpt-4.1-mini for this structured branch-control router were capability-safe and much cheaper/faster than the baseline gpt-5.5 routing; candidate-1 also achieved the best aggregate quality, so retain mini here.
rationale.generate_answer: Candidate-2 showed that moving final answer generation from gpt-5.5 to gpt-4.1-mini cut cost/latency but reduced exact match/F1 versus candidate-1. Restore gpt-5.5 for this user-facing quality-critical unit to probe quality recovery while keeping other units inexpensive.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: This unit requires tool calling and branch control and is the highest-frequency call site. gpt-4.1-mini supports tool calling, was validated in candidates 1-2, and delivered large cost/latency savings over baseline gpt-5.5.
rationale.rewrite_question: Prior candidates assigned rewrite to qwen-local, but observed no rewrite invocations, leaving its impact untested. Assigning gpt-4.1-mini is still low cost, supports the needed context, and may be more reliable than the 2B local model if the rewrite branch is exercised, without paying gpt-5.5 rewrite costs.

plan.description: Local-router cost probe: retain the empirically best quality-critical gpt-5.5 final answer generation, keep gpt-4.1-mini for the high-frequency tool-calling initial retrieval controller, and move the structured retrieval sufficiency router plus rewrite path to qwen-local to test whether local branch control can reduce remaining routing cloud cost while preserving candidate-1/3 answer quality characteristics.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This non-user-facing router requires structured output and branch control; qwen-local explicitly supports structured output and has sufficient context. Candidates 1-3 showed gpt-4.1-mini routing was cheap and effective, but this unit still accounted for roughly $0.04-$0.047 and ~46-48s aggregate latency. Moving it local is a capability-safe way to explore further cloud-cost reduction and possible latency trade-offs, while accepting some routing-quality risk.
rationale.generate_answer: Keep gpt-5.5-cloud for final answer generation because candidate-2's all-mini answer step cut cost but reduced exact match/F1, while candidates 1 and 3 recovered the best observed aggregate quality with gpt-5.5 here. This isolates the effect of local retrieval sufficiency routing without also weakening answer synthesis.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: Use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud because this highest-frequency structural unit requires tool calling and branch control. Candidates 1-3 validated that gpt-4.1-mini supports the endpoint capabilities and greatly reduces cost/latency versus baseline gpt-5.5 while maintaining strong retrieval behavior.
rationale.rewrite_question: Use qwen-local for this non-user-facing, no-tool, unstructured rewrite step. Prior runs saw no rewrite invocations, so local assignment is unlikely to affect common paths, and if exercised it avoids gpt-5.5 rewrite cost while remaining within context/capability constraints.

plan.description: Tool-controller locality probe: keep the best-observed quality-critical gpt-5.5 final answer generation and the validated low-cost gpt-4.1-mini structured retrieval router, but move the high-frequency initial retrieval controller to qwen-local to test whether local tool-calling can reduce remaining cloud cost despite possible branch/tool-routing latency and quality risk; keep rewrite local because it is non-user-facing and has not been exercised in prior runs.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: Use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for this structured branch-control router. Candidates 1-3 validated mini as capability-safe and fast/cheap for structured routing, with better latency than the local-router candidate-4 where qwen-local increased aggregate router latency substantially. This isolates the new experiment to the initial tool controller rather than also changing sufficiency routing.
rationale.generate_answer: Retain gpt-5.5-cloud for final answer generation because candidates 1, 3, and 4 all showed stronger exact match/F1 when gpt-5.5 handled the user-facing final answer, while candidate-2's all-mini final answer reduced cost but degraded quality. Keeping gpt-5.5 here protects answer synthesis while testing a different cost lever.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: Move this highest-frequency tool-calling branch-control unit to qwen-local. qwen-local explicitly supports tool calling and has sufficient context, and prior runs show this unit contributes recurring cloud cost under gpt-4.1-mini (~$0.05-$0.06). This previously unevaluated assignment probes maximum cloud-cost reduction on the controller path, accepting risk that the 2B local model may produce poorer tool/answer routing or higher latency.
rationale.rewrite_question: Assign qwen-local for the non-user-facing rewrite step. It requires no tool calling or structured output, has sufficient context locally, and prior candidates with local/cloud rewrite saw no rewrite invocations, so local placement remains the lowest-cost safe default if the branch is rarely or never used.

plan.description: Latency/cost-focused all-mini cloud with stronger cloud rewrite coverage: use gpt-4.1-mini for all non-rewrite and rewrite units, including the high-frequency tool controller and structured sufficiency router, to revisit the very low-latency/cost profile of candidate-2 while removing the local rewrite assignment so the rare rewrite path (which appeared once in candidate-5) is handled by a more capable low-cost cloud model.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: gpt-4.1-mini-cloud is capability-safe for structured output and branch control, and prior candidates using it for this router had low aggregate latency (~46-48s) and minimal cost (~$0.04-$0.047), outperforming the local-router latency seen in candidate-4.
rationale.generate_answer: Switching answer generation to gpt-4.1-mini repeats the low-cost answer-synthesis lever from candidate-2, which achieved the best latency and lowest cost among evaluated plans, while accepting potential quality loss versus gpt-5.5; this is useful to map the cost/latency frontier.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: This unit requires tool calling and branch control. gpt-4.1-mini has been validated across candidates 1-4 as reliable, cheap, and fast for this high-frequency controller; qwen-local in candidate-5 reduced cloud cost but increased latency and reduced quality, so this proposal returns the controller to mini.
rationale.rewrite_question: Prior all-mini-like candidate-2 left rewrite on qwen-local and saw no rewrite calls, while candidate-5 showed the rewrite branch can be exercised once and local rewrite was slow. gpt-4.1-mini is low-cost, has ample context, and should provide safer rewrite behavior than qwen-local without using expensive gpt-5.5.

plan.description: Expensive-router quality probe: keep gpt-4.1-mini for the high-frequency tool-calling initial controller to preserve the validated low-cost retrieval entry path, keep gpt-5.5 for final answer generation because it consistently improves answer quality, and move only the structured retrieval sufficiency router to gpt-5.5 while leaving rewrite local. This tests whether stronger post-retrieval branch decisions recover/support candidate-4-level quality or improve title recall without paying baseline cost on every unit.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: Prior best-quality hybrids used either gpt-4.1-mini or qwen-local here. Candidate-4 with qwen-local slightly improved exact match/F1 but increased latency; candidates 1/3 with mini were cheaper/faster and strong. This previously unevaluated placement assigns gpt-5.5 to the structured post-retrieval router to test whether stronger sufficiency/branch decisions improve routing quality and supporting-title behavior while avoiding baseline's expensive gpt-5.5 initial controller and rewrite usage. gpt-5.5 supports the required structured output and branch control.
rationale.generate_answer: Retain gpt-5.5-cloud for the user-facing final answer because candidate-2/6 all-mini answer generation was much cheaper/faster but reduced exact match and F1, whereas candidates 1, 3, 4, and 5 recovered better quality with gpt-5.5 at this unit.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: Use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for this high-frequency structural unit requiring tool calling. It has been validated in candidates 1-4 and 6 as capability-safe, fast, and very low cost compared with baseline gpt-5.5; qwen-local in candidate-5 reduced cloud cost but hurt latency and quality, so mini is the better controller trade-off for this probe.
rationale.rewrite_question: Assign qwen-local because this non-user-facing rewrite requires no tool calling or structured output and has rarely or never been invoked in most runs. Candidate-5 showed local rewrite can be slow if used, but keeping it local avoids extra gpt-5.5 cost on a low-frequency path and makes this experiment isolate the value of the stronger retrieval sufficiency router.

plan.description: Full-local capability probe: assign qwen-local to every placement unit to measure the zero-cloud-cost endpoint across tool calling, structured post-retrieval routing, answer generation, and rewriting. This is a previously unevaluated extreme point on the cost frontier, contrasting with prior local-router and local-controller partial probes while respecting all declared endpoint capabilities.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This unit requires structured output and branch control; qwen-local explicitly supports structured output and was capability-safe when used for this router in candidate-4. Candidate-4 achieved the best exact_match/F1 among evaluated plans despite higher local-router latency, so an all-local run can test whether routing remains acceptable when paired with local controller and answer generation, while eliminating router cloud cost entirely.
rationale.generate_answer: This is the highest quality-risk change because prior mini answer generation reduced quality versus gpt-5.5, and qwen-local is smaller than mini. However, no evaluated plan has tested local final answer generation. Assigning qwen-local here maps the zero-cloud-cost extreme and determines whether retrieved-context extractive answers can be produced adequately by the local model, accepting likely quality loss for cost exploration.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: This structural entry unit requires tool calling and branch control; qwen-local declares tool_calling support and was capability-safe in candidate-5. Candidate-5 showed local controller increased latency and reduced quality relative to mini, but it also reduced cloud cost. Keeping it local here completes the zero-cloud-cost experiment and tests interactions with local routing/answering rather than isolating only the controller.
rationale.rewrite_question: The rewrite step is non-user-facing and requires neither tools nor structured output. qwen-local has been used for rewrite in multiple prior candidates, including one observed invocation in candidate-5, with no validation failures. Local rewrite maintains zero cloud spend on the rare retry path.

plan.description: Cloud-strong controller with local router: keep gpt-5.5 only for final answer generation, move the high-frequency initial tool-calling controller back to gpt-5.5 to test whether stronger first-hop retrieval/query decisions recover quality lost in local-controller and expensive-router probes, and use qwen-local for the structured post-retrieval sufficiency router plus rewrite to reduce cloud spend relative to baseline while exploring a previously unevaluated quality/cost/latency point.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: qwen-local supports structured output and has sufficient context for this non-user-facing branch-control router. Candidate-4 showed local post-retrieval routing was capability-safe and yielded the best observed aggregate exact match/F1, though with higher router latency; keeping it local reduces cloud cost versus gpt-4.1-mini/gpt-5.5 routing and distinguishes this proposal from prior mini-router and expensive-router configurations.
rationale.generate_answer: Use gpt-5.5-cloud for the user-facing final answer. Runs with gpt-5.5 answer generation (candidates 1, 3, 4) consistently outperformed all-mini and all-local answer generation on exact match/F1, while candidate-4 in particular paired gpt-5.5 answering with local routing for the current best aggregate quality.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: Assign gpt-5.5-cloud to this structural tool-calling entry controller. Prior runs validated gpt-4.1-mini as cheap/fast and qwen-local as cost-saving but lower quality/higher latency; this previously unevaluated setting tests whether the strongest model's initial retrieval/tool decisions improve retrieval sufficiency and downstream answer quality enough to justify higher controller cost, while still avoiding baseline's gpt-5.5 post-retrieval router and rewrite cost.
rationale.rewrite_question: Use qwen-local for this rare, non-user-facing rewrite path that requires neither tool calling nor structured output. It has been capability-safe in earlier candidates and keeps retry/rewrite cloud cost at zero; any quality risk is isolated to a low-frequency branch.

plan.description: Mini answer with strongest cloud entry controller and local post-retrieval router: test whether gpt-5.5 initial tool/query decisions can improve retrieval while keeping final synthesis inexpensive, and use qwen-local for structured sufficiency routing plus rare rewrite to reduce cloud cost versus baseline and candidate-9. This is a previously unevaluated placement distinct from all prior assignment maps.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: qwen-local supports structured output and has sufficient context for this non-user-facing branch-control router. Candidate-4 showed local sufficiency routing can be capability-safe and even competitive on aggregate answer quality when paired with strong answering, although it increases latency; retaining it here avoids the expensive gpt-5.5 router cost seen in baseline/candidate-7 and isolates the effect of a stronger initial controller with cheaper final answering.
rationale.generate_answer: Use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for final answer generation to explore a lower-cost/lower-latency synthesis trade-off. Candidate-2/6 showed mini answer generation gives very low cost and latency but lower quality than gpt-5.5; pairing it with gpt-5.5 initial retrieval control and local post-retrieval routing is unevaluated and tests whether improved first-hop retrieval can offset some answer-synthesis weakness while keeping cost below gpt-5.5-answer hybrids.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: Assign gpt-5.5-cloud to the high-frequency structural entry controller requiring tool calling and branch control. Candidate-9 tried this stronger controller with gpt-5.5 answering and local routing but quality/cost were poor; this proposal changes the answer unit to mini to map whether the expensive controller has any retrieval benefit under a much cheaper final-answer regime. gpt-5.5 satisfies tool-calling and context requirements.
rationale.rewrite_question: Use qwen-local for the rare non-user-facing rewrite path, which requires no tool calling or structured output. It has been capability-safe in earlier candidates and keeps retry/rewrite cloud cost at zero; any latency/quality risk is confined to a low-frequency branch.

plan.description: Strong-cloud entry with validated mini post-retrieval support: use gpt-5.5 for the quality-critical initial tool/query controller and final answer generation, while keeping the structured sufficiency router and rare rewrite path on gpt-4.1-mini to avoid the local-router latency/quality instability and reduce cost versus the all-gpt-5.5 baseline. This previously unevaluated map probes whether stronger first-hop retrieval decisions can help when paired with the best answer generator, without also paying for gpt-5.5 routing/rewrite.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: Assign gpt-4.1-mini-cloud because it supports structured output and branch-control requirements and was consistently capability-safe in candidates 1, 2, 3, 5, and 6. The expensive gpt-5.5 router in candidate-7 increased cost/latency without quality gains, while qwen-local routing in candidate-4 was sometimes strong but slower and unstable in later strong-controller variants; mini is the more balanced post-retrieval router for this probe.
rationale.generate_answer: Use gpt-5.5-cloud for final answer generation because evaluated runs with gpt-5.5 answering generally dominated mini/local answering on exact match and F1, with candidate-4 reaching the best observed aggregate quality and candidates 1/3 also strong. This preserves the quality-critical user-facing synthesis step while other placements test routing trade-offs.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: Assign gpt-5.5-cloud to the initial retrieval controller to explore whether the strongest tool-capable model can improve first-hop query/tool decisions when not paired with the slower local post-retrieval router used in candidates 9 and 10. This unit requires tool calling and branch control, both supported by gpt-5.5; the placement is deliberately a quality-oriented cost/latency trade-off compared with mini-controller candidates.
rationale.rewrite_question: Use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for rewrite_question. The branch is rare but has been observed, and candidate-5 showed local rewrite can be slow. Mini has ample context, low cost, and should be more reliable than qwen-local for query reformulation, while avoiding the high gpt-5.5 rewrite costs from the baseline.

plan.description: Best-quality hybrid with cloud rewrite safety: keep the candidate-4 pattern that produced the strongest observed aggregate exact match/F1 by using qwen-local for structured post-retrieval sufficiency routing, gpt-5.5 for final answer generation, and gpt-4.1-mini for the high-frequency initial tool controller; change only the rare rewrite path from local to gpt-4.1-mini to reduce rewrite latency/quality risk if that branch is exercised while remaining far cheaper than all-gpt-5.5.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: qwen-local supports the required structured output and has already been capability-safe for this branch-control router. Candidate-4, which used local post-retrieval routing with gpt-5.5 answering and mini initial control, achieved the best observed exact_match (0.66) and answer F1 (~0.781), suggesting the local router is worth re-testing despite higher router latency.
rationale.generate_answer: Retain gpt-5.5-cloud for the user-facing final answer because runs with gpt-5.5 answer generation consistently outperformed mini/local answer generation on aggregate quality; candidate-2/6 all-mini answers were much cheaper and faster but had lower exact match/F1, and all-local answering degraded substantially.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: Use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for the high-frequency structural entry controller requiring tool calling. It has been validated across multiple runs as capability-safe, low-cost, and faster than gpt-5.5, while qwen-local in candidate-5 increased latency and reduced quality. This preserves the proven controller trade-off from candidates 1, 3, and 4.
rationale.rewrite_question: Switch rewrite_question to gpt-4.1-mini-cloud rather than qwen-local. The branch is rare, but candidate-5 and candidate-7 show rewrite can be invoked and local rewrite can be slow; mini is low-cost, has ample context, and should be more reliable for reformulation without paying gpt-5.5 rewrite cost. This assignment map has not been evaluated previously.
